questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: To see Canada’s nature.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was required GPA and language proficiency given that many want you to take a form of exam to prove your proficiency, but that costs a lot of money. Didn’t wanna do that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a good experience with beautiful nature to observe. Made a few friends to travel with, and have fun with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get an info mail, which explained very nicely how to get around and choose courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I lived on campus, so I got mail on where to go to get keys to my room. The receptionist helped me, and told me about the placed. I was then driven by a taxi to my dorm (for free). The people at the dorm helped explain how things were around there and where important things were, like shopping markets and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could choose between Alumni house or Bayfield hall. I chose Alumni house because you then get a suite with three other exchange students but you get your own room. I Bayfield you share a room with another person.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were meal plans, I didn’t choose a meal plan and that worked fine - wasn’t too expensive, about the same as in Denmark. I know one who had a meal plan and she got totally scammed. Half of the meal plan money goes to the people working in the cafeteria. So you only have half of the meal plan money to live for for four months, and the food in the cafeteria is expensive. For one meal you use about 70-100 kr. depending on how food you get and how much it weighs.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very nice to live on campus, no need for public transport - even though the transport is free because of your student card. And from Alumni it only took 15 minutes walking to the center of campus.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don’t remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I know you could email the exchange service on Western University to get help about courses and such, because I used it many times to know if I could have this course or not.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful, but I finally got some courses that I wanted but it took some time and patience.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t expect to get the course, when you read about it. Even if you think that you could totally make it, but if they deem that you can’t, you don’t get the course and then you have to find a new course. Very frustrating.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was kinda gymnasium and first-year university level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You had to memorize it all for the exams, and it is multiple choice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PSYCHOL 1002A - Psychological as a Natural Science.
ANATCELL 2200A - Systemic Anatomy of the Human Body.
MICROIMM 2500A - Biology of Infection and Immunity.
BIOCHEM 3381A - Protein Structures and Enzymes.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PSYCHOL 1002A is my recommendation if you want to take an easy course, but still learn something at your own pace. It is an online course, the lectures are pre-recorded and the exam (multiple choice) is also over the computer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of clubs and social things, especially in the summer with OWeek (orientation week), homecoming, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Outdoor club. I didn’t go on any of their trips, but you can rent materials like backpacks, sleeping packs, etc. for free. It was very nice if you want to go backpacking in Canada, which I highly recommend if you really want to see the kind of nature that Canada has to offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see an American football game (Western Mustangs are really good) and ice hockey game (not so good, but still nice the experience). You also get a whole week free at the end of October to start November, which I highly recommend going to Vancouver and experience the nature around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, much similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, didn’t really talk with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that I can remember.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No idea.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Remember a converter.
2) If you have an iPad, take it with you. It makes it so easier to take notes during the lectures. Every local student have an iPad or a computer with a touch screen.
3) Even though that it is called “study abroad”, see the country. It is so beautiful with its mountains and lakes.

questions.answer: Not a clue.
